## Week 5 – OpenLoom (ESP32 History Flashcard Device)

### What I worked on
OpenLoom is a pocket History flashcard device built around an ESP32. It has an OLED screen, 2 buttons (next / reveal) and a buzzer for feedback. This session I [wired up the OLED and buttons / wrote the card-flip logic / tested the buzzer / cleaned up the repo].

### What I built
- [Show the question on the OLED and reveal the answer with a button press]
- [Button debouncing so one press equals one action]
- [Buzzer beep on reveal / next card]
- [Repo checks all passing on GitHub]

### What broke and how I fixed it
- [Problem, e.g. OLED stayed blank → I had the wrong I2C address, fixed it after scanning]
- [Problem, e.g. buttons triggered twice → added a debounce delay]

### What's next
- [Add more History cards (topics from my B.A. course)]
- [Add a score / streak counter]
- [Take final photos of the device and finish the README]

**Repo:** https://github.com/bidyutdolui1970-cpu/openloom

### 2026-11-08: ## What I worked on

**2h**

## What I worked on
This session I worked on the hardware side of OpenLoom, my ESP32 History flashcard device (OLED, 2 buttons, buzzer). I focused on the enclosure design and getting the project files organized in the repo.

## What I built
- Added the OpenLoom firmware, parts list, documentation and images to the repo
- Added the enclosure CAD files and the KiCad schematic
- Fixed the enclosure lid, the screw bores and the overall height so the parts fit properly
- Exported and added a STEP file for the enclosure, so it can be opened in any CAD tool or 3D printed
- Synced the project from Half Life into the repo

## What went wrong and how I fixed it
- The first enclosure design had problems with the lid, the screw bores and the height, so I corrected those dimensions in CAD
- [Add anything else that actually broke for you]

## What I learned
- How to design an enclosure around real components
- How to draw a schematic in KiCad
- How to export a STEP file and keep hardware files organized in Git

## What's next
- Test-fit the real parts in the enclosure
- Add more History questions to the firmware
- Record a timelapse of the final build
